summary.business_type: Content publisher / affiliate blog (home decor niche, Pinterest-driven traffic, matched Fourthwall POD store)
top_findings: Zero structured data (schema.org) on homepage, /about, /blog listing, category pages, and legal pages -- only the 50 blog posts carry BlogPosting/FAQPage/Breadcrumb schema
No security headers beyond HSTS -- missing X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy
Unoptimized images: all hero/inline images are raw .jpg (150-170KB each), no WebP/AVIF, PageSpeed flags ~1,985 KiB of potential savings and 2,875 KiB total page weight on the homepage
Mobile LCP measured at 4.1s (needs-improvement threshold is 2.5s) via live PageSpeed Insights -- confirms the image-weight finding is a real user-facing issue, not just a lab warning
No llms.txt and no AI-crawler-specific signals -- AI Search Readiness gap on a site whose content (first-person, AUD-priced, source-specific) is otherwise well-suited to AI citation
quick_wins: Naive https://outdoorcoastalhome.com/sitemap.xml serves the site's 404 page instead of the real sitemap (real one is only reachable via sitemap-index.xml -> sitemap-0.xml) -- add a redirect or make /sitemap.xml itself valid, since many tools/crawlers probe that path by default
Add Organization/WebSite JSON-LD to the homepage and WebPage schema to /about, /blog, and the legal pages -- near-zero effort, currently completely absent outside blog posts
Add the 5 missing security response headers via Vercel config (vercel.json headers) -- a few lines, no code risk
Convert hero/inline images to WebP/AVIF (or route through Astro's built-in image optimization instead of static /images/ raw files) -- directly fixes the flagged 1,985 KiB PageSpeed savings
Create a minimal llms.txt at the root -- near-zero effort, immediate AI-crawler signal

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: robots.txt correctly allows all and points to sitemap-index.xml
sitemap-index.xml -> sitemap-0.xml resolves cleanly with 56 URLs, all 200-status
www -> apex and http -> https both 308-redirect correctly to canonical https://outdoorcoastalhome.com/
Real 404s return true 404 status codes (verified on a nonexistent blog slug)
Canonical tags present and self-referential and correct on every page checked
HSTS header present (max-age=63072000)

findings.title: /sitemap.xml resolves to the site's 404 page, not the sitemap
findings.description: Requesting https://outdoorcoastalhome.com/sitemap.xml returns the rendered 'Page Not Found' HTML page (200 status, ~37KB) instead of XML or a redirect. The functioning sitemap only exists at /sitemap-index.xml -> /sitemap-0.xml. robots.txt correctly references sitemap-index.xml so GSC discovery is fine, but any tool, plugin, or crawler that defaults to checking /sitemap.xml (very common convention) will silently fail.
findings.recommendation: Add a redirect from /sitemap.xml to /sitemap-index.xml, or generate /sitemap.xml directly as the index file.

findings.title: Missing security response headers
findings.description: Only Strict-Transport-Security is present on responses. No X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy headers were observed on the homepage or any sampled page.
findings.recommendation: Add a headers() block in vercel.json (or Astro middleware) setting X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY/SAMEORIGIN, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and a baseline CSP.

findings.title: No llms.txt
findings.description: https://outdoorcoastalhome.com/llms.txt returns 404. No explicit AI-crawler guidance file exists.
findings.recommendation: Add a minimal llms.txt listing the site's purpose, key pages, and permitted-use note -- low effort, aligns with the AI Search Readiness gap noted below.

findings.title: Category and tag URLs indexed alongside canonical blog posts
findings.description: The sitemap includes /blog/category/hamptons-style (a thin listing page) and blog posts link out to /blog?tag=... query-string filter URLs. These add index bloat and dilution risk without unique value.
findings.recommendation: Either build out category pages with genuinely unique intro copy + noindex thin ones, and add rel=canonical or noindex on ?tag= filter views so they don't compete with the main /blog listing.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: Blog posts sampled run 3,100-4,500 words -- not thin content

Strong first-person E-E-A-T signals: 'I've had a Gold Coast pergola for 4 years', specific AUD prices, named Australian retailers (Temple & Webster, Beacon Lighting, Dulux/Taubmans paint codes) -- reads as genuinely experienced, not generic AI filler
Named author (Badreddine Br) consistently attributed via Person schema and linked to an /about page
Editorial Policy page exists, which is a real E-E-A-T/trust signal many niche blogs skip

findings.title: Author bio lacks depth/credentials
findings.description: The /about page identifies the author by name but doesn't establish specific credentials, location detail, or a track record beyond general interest -- thinner than ideal for E-E-A-T given Google's continued scrutiny of affiliate/decor content.
findings.recommendation: Expand /about with concrete specifics (which Australian city/region, how many projects/homes, any relevant background) mirroring the specificity already used inside the posts themselves.

findings.title: Category pages are thin listings
findings.description: /blog/category/hamptons-style is a short auto-generated listing with generic intro copy, indexed via sitemap but with far less unique content than the main posts.
findings.recommendation: Either add unique curatorial copy per category (a few hundred words explaining the category, not just links) or exclude these from the sitemap.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Every sampled page has a unique, keyword-relevant title tag and meta description
Single H1 per page, consistent heading hierarchy
Canonical tags correct and self-referential
Decent internal linking: ~9 contextual internal links per post sampled, plus category/tag links

findings.title: Static/legal pages share a generic OG image
findings.description: /about, /blog, /privacy-policy, /terms-of-use, and the homepage all reuse the same og:image (unsplash-1600566753086...jpg) instead of a purpose-built social image, weakening social-share click-through.
findings.recommendation: Generate a branded OG/social image for the homepage and a generic branded fallback distinct from a random Unsplash photo.

categories.name: Schema / Structured Data
what_works: Blog posts (sampled: 8/8) carry a complete, well-formed schema graph: BlogPosting, FAQPage + Question/Answer, BreadcrumbList, Person (author), Organization (publisher), ImageObject, WebPage
FAQPage schema is genuinely tied to on-page FAQ content, not fabricated

findings.title: No schema at all on non-post pages
findings.description: Homepage, /about, /blog listing, /editorial-policy, /privacy-policy, /terms-of-use all returned zero @type schema matches. Only individual blog posts have structured data.
findings.recommendation: Add WebSite + Organization JSON-LD to the homepage (enables sitelinks search box eligibility and consistent entity signals), and WebPage/AboutPage/CollectionPage schema to the remaining static pages.

categories.name: Performance (CWV)
what_works: Lighthouse mobile scores (live PageSpeed Insights, homepage): Performance 83, Accessibility 96, Best Practices 100, SEO 100
Cumulative Layout Shift excellent: 0.002
Total Blocking Time low: 150ms

findings.title: Largest Contentful Paint at 4.1s (mobile, homepage) -- needs-improvement threshold
findings.description: Live PageSpeed Insights data (not lab estimate) puts mobile LCP at 4.1s, above Google's 2.5s 'good' threshold and near the 4.0s 'poor' boundary. 'Improve image delivery' flagged at ~1,985 KiB potential savings; total page weight 2,875 KiB.
findings.recommendation: Serve hero images as WebP/AVIF at appropriately sized dimensions (route through Astro's built-in <Image> optimization rather than static /images/*.jpg files), and consider a CDN image resizer.

findings.title: No CrUX field data available
findings.description: Chrome UX Report has no data for this origin yet -- expected for a low-traffic, recently-reactivated site, not itself a problem, but means Core Web Vitals field scores can't be verified until traffic grows.
findings.recommendation: Re-check CrUX in 60-90 days once traffic volume is sufficient.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness (GEO)
what_works: FAQPage schema with real Q&A content on every blog post is a strong AI-citation structural asset already in place
Answer-first, specific, sourced content (prices, named retailers) is exactly the kind of passage AI Overviews/Perplexity prefer to cite

findings.title: No llms.txt, no explicit AI-crawler allowlist beyond default robots.txt
findings.description: robots.txt is a blanket Allow: / with no AI-specific user-agent guidance (GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot etc. all inherit the same generic allow, which is functionally fine, but there's no llms.txt to summarize the site for AI crawlers).
findings.recommendation: Add llms.txt; consider explicit AI-bot allow lines in robots.txt for clarity.

categories.name: Images
what_works: Alt text present and descriptive on 100% of images sampled across all pages checked (0 missing alt attributes)
Hero images use loading="eager" + fetchpriority="high" correctly for LCP images; below-fold images use loading="lazy"

findings.title: All images are unoptimized raw JPEG, no responsive srcset
findings.description: Every image sampled (hero + inline) is served as a flat .jpg at 150-170KB+ with a single fixed size, no srcset/sizes attributes, no WebP/AVIF variant. This is the direct cause of the PageSpeed 'Improve image delivery' warning (~1,985 KiB) and contributes to the 4.1s LCP.
findings.recommendation: Route images through Astro's built-in image pipeline (astro:assets) to auto-generate WebP/AVIF + responsive srcset instead of serving static files from /public/images/ directly.

phases.name: Phase 1: Critical Fixes
items: Fix /sitemap.xml to redirect to /sitemap-index.xml instead of serving the 404 page
Add security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, baseline CSP) via vercel.json

phases.name: Phase 2: High-Impact Improvements
items: Convert site images to WebP/AVIF with responsive srcset (Astro image pipeline) to cut the 1,985 KiB PageSpeed penalty and bring mobile LCP under 2.5s
Add WebSite/Organization JSON-LD to homepage and WebPage schema to /about, /blog, and legal pages

phases.name: Phase 3: Content & Authority
items: Expand /about with concrete author credentials/specifics to strengthen E-E-A-T
Add unique curatorial copy to category pages or exclude thin ones from the sitemap
Set up GSC + GA4 API access for outdoorcoastalhome.com (currently not configured) to unlock real indexation/traffic data for future audits

phases.name: Phase 4: Monitoring & Iteration
items: Re-run PageSpeed Insights after image optimization ships to confirm LCP improvement
Re-check CrUX field data in 60-90 days once traffic accumulates
Re-audit after GSC/GA4 access is live to replace lab estimates with real indexation and query data
